title: EICV7 priority-file structural report

method.metadata: Used pyreadstat metadata-only inspection for labels and value-label dictionaries.
method.record_grain_checks: Read only selected ID/item columns, one file at a time, to test uniqueness and overlap; no complete dataset was loaded.

household_id_candidate.label: Household Identification
household_id_candidate.evidence: Unique and nonmissing in both household-shaped files (15,054 rows each). Each priority file contains the same 15,054 distinct hhid values; hhid repeats in person and item/transaction files.
household_id_candidate.assessment: Strong internal household-key candidate; uniqueness is grain-dependent and this is not a merge authorization.

person_id_candidate.evidence: The person roster has 62,110 nonmissing, unique hhid-pid pairs. pid alone takes only 16 values (1-16), so it is a within-household member number, not a project-wide unique ID.

related_file_checks.CS_S9D5_Financial_Services.dta: 333 nonmissing hhid-pid pairs; all 333 match the person roster. The other 14,721 pid values are missing.
related_file_checks.CS_S10A1_A2_credits.dta: 12,639 distinct nonmissing hhid-pid pairs; all match the person roster. No orphan member rows among the checked nonmissing pairs.
related_file_checks.CS_S10C_Savings.dta: 27,348 distinct nonmissing hhid-pid pairs; 27,347 match the person roster and one does not. Investigate before relying on this link.

person_id_candidate.assessment: Strong within-EICV7 member-link candidate based on labels and observed key matches; confirm identifiers and file relationships in survey documentation before joining.

cluster_candidate.label: Clust
cluster_candidate.assessment: Likely survey cluster/PSU identifier based on name and presence across all seven files; confirm its design role from survey documentation.

geographic_fields.province: Province code; value labels identify the five provinces.
geographic_fields.district: District code; value labels identify districts.

survey_design_fields.weight: Labelled Household Weight; present in all seven files.
survey_design_fields.pop_wt: Labelled Population Weight; present in the poverty and household files only.
survey_design_fields.strata_id: Present in the household, person, access, financial-services, credits, and savings files; absent from the poverty file.
survey_design_fields.caution: Weights repeat on person/item/transaction rows. Do not treat a repeated household weight as a row-level weight or select a weighting strategy before confirming the survey design and analysis unit.

poverty_fields_repeated_across_files.caution: These outcome-like fields are present in all seven priority files, not just the poverty file. Their presence in a joined table creates direct leakage risk for poverty targets.

s1q2.3: Son or daughter of household head

files.grain_evidence: hhid is nonmissing and unique for all 15,054 rows; its household-ID set matches the other six priority files.
files.relation_to_other_files: Household-level outcome/consumption table; shares the full hhid universe with the household file and all other priority files.

files.grain_evidence: hhid is nonmissing and unique for all 15,054 rows; exact hhid set match with the poverty file and other priority files.
files.relation_to_other_files: Household-level questionnaire content; this file's unique hhid roster is the internal reference used for the ID coverage checks.

files.grain_evidence: 62,110 unique, nonmissing (hhid,pid) pairs across 15,054 households; pid alone repeats as member numbers 1-16.
person_and_demographic_variables: s1q2 (Relation with the head of household)
financial_service_variables: s4bq23c (uses mobile financial services: MOMO/Airtel Money/Mocash/push and pull)
files.relation_to_other_files: The roster is the person-link candidate for nonmissing hhid-pid references in the financial-services, credit, and savings files.

files.grain_evidence: 15,054 households x 15 service codes = 225,810 rows; all 15 codes occur and there are no duplicate hhid-s5fq0 pairs.
files.relation_to_other_files: Household IDs cover the same 15,054 households, but each household expands to one record for each of 15 basic-service categories.

files.likely_grain: Household-level VUP financial-service module, with sparse member reference
files.grain_evidence: One row per unique hhid. pid is labelled ID HH Member but is nonmissing in only 333 rows; all 333 hhid-pid pairs match the person roster.

person: pid, labelled ID HH Member; sparse member-reference candidate

financial_service_variables: s9d5q1 (household ever applied for financial-service loan)
credit_variables: s9d5q1-s9d5q7 (VUP financial-service loan application/approval and details)
files.relation_to_other_files: Same household roster. Sparse pid references match roster pairs where present; do not treat pid as the row key.

files.likely_grain: Household/member/loan record, with screening or no-loan rows possible
files.grain_evidence: 15,054 distinct hhid values; 12,639 distinct nonmissing hhid-pid pairs all match the person roster. Candidate (hhid,pid,s10aq4) has no duplicate rows. 4,739 rows have both pid and s10aq4 missing.
credit_variables: s10aq1 (member tried to obtain a loan)
files.relation_to_other_files: Household IDs match the roster; nonmissing member references match the person file. Multiple rows per household and the loan ID field suggest loan/member records, while blank member/loan IDs indicate a screening or non-loan record type that needs questionnaire documentation.

files.grain_evidence: 15,054 distinct hhid values. Candidate (hhid,pid,s10cq3) has no duplicate rows; pid is missing in 753 rows and account ID s10cq3 is missing in 6. One distinct nonmissing hhid-pid pair does not match the person roster.
files.relation_to_other_files: Household IDs match the roster and most member references match the person file. The single unmatched hhid-pid pair is unresolved; the candidate account/member composite needs codebook confirmation.

relational_assessment.household_primary_key_candidate: hhid; verified unique at household grain in the poverty and household files, and common across the full household universe in all seven files.
relational_assessment.person_member_key_candidate: (hhid,pid); verified unique in the person roster. pid is not globally unique and should not be used alone.
item_or_transaction_level_files: CS_S10A1_A2_credits.dta (member/loan records plus rows with missing member/loan IDs)
relational_assessment.linkage_status: Within-EICV7 hhid coverage is identical across these files; member pair checks support internal roster references. No merge was performed. This says nothing about record-level linkage to FinScope.

leakage_and_interpretation_risks: For poverty outcomes, exclude poverty labels copied into other files (poverty, pov_jan, epov_jan, quintile) and direct construction/derivative variables such as cons1, cons1ae, sol_jan, food, exp1-exp11, and poverty lines unless the task is explicitly descriptive rather than predictive.

For account-ownership targets, s10cq1 and s10cq4 overlap with the target concept; institution, account type, interest, and tontine fields may define or occur downstream of ownership. Do not use them without a target-specific leakage review.

For s9d5q2 loan approval, s9d5q3-s9d5q7 describe receipt and approved-loan details and are post-application/outcome candidates for leakage. Their timing and questionnaire skip logic need confirmation.

Person, service, credit, and savings files repeat household-level poverty fields and weights across rows. Joining them can duplicate household labels/weights and change the analytical unit or class balance.
The code labels provide category meanings, but survey documentation is still needed to confirm skip patterns, sampling/weight use, cluster/strata definitions, and intended key semantics.
open_checks_before_constructing_an_analy: Confirm hhid/pid/account/loan key definitions and questionnaire universes in the EICV7 codebook; investigate the one unmatched savings hhid-pid pair.
Confirm the design role and intended use of weight, pop_wt, strata_id, and clust for each analysis unit.
Confirm whether repeated poverty/weight fields are supplied for convenience or generated at a particular household/person grain before selecting source tables.
